mrd.text: Mirrodin began as the artificial plane Argentum, which Karn left in the care of his warden Memnarch, granting him the Mirari orb and stewardship of the plane.
A spot of glistening oil caught Memnarch's eye and corrupted him; he renamed the world Mirrodin, terraformed it, destroyed the ur-golems and began abducting inhabitants of other planes.
Bruenna united the races of Mirrodin with Glissa and Lyese against Memnarch, and when Slobad relinquished his spark the Vanishing recovered the souls.

dst.text: On Mirrodin, Memnarch's work was bringing the plane to life, and it began to take on a life of its own.
Memnarch created the myr to be dependable, controllable and disposable, and he escalated the stakes whenever the plane's civilizations found ways to fight his levelers.
Glissa, fleeing vedalken pursuers, discovered that Memnarch was real, and his plan was revealed: he would use the green sun's power and Glissa's spark to become a planeswalker.

5dn.text: Mirrodin's fifth sun was born, seen by some as doom and by others as salvation, and it joined the other four and awakened new abilities in the plane's creatures.
Glissa, Bosh and Slobad journeyed to the core with the Kaldra avatar to confront Memnarch, but he seized it with a single spell and turned it on them.
Glissa threw herself at Memnarch so that both fell into the mana core, her spark transferred to Slobad, and Karn returned.
Karn restored the souls, causing the Vanishing, and gave the Mirari to Glissa, Slobad and Geth.

som.text: After Memnarch's defeat, Mirrodin's older generations were sent back to their home planes, leaving a generation of Mirran orphans.
Unknown to anyone, Karn carried Phyrexian oil in his heartstone and left traces of it on Mirrodin, planting a virus through which Phyrexia secretly began rebuilding itself.
Phyrexia then invaded and tarnished the plane, creating a conflict with the native Mirrans, and Venser gave his spark and heart to Karn so he could vow to stop the Phyrexians.

mbs.text: Mirrodin's Phyrexian assault intensified while the Mirran resistance rallied.
Elspeth freed Melira, who was immune to phyresis, and Melira healed the infected rebels at Ezuri's camp.
Venser gave his life and spark to Karn, releasing him from Phyrexian tyranny, while Glissa was accused by the elves and eventually corrupted by Vorinclex.
Elesh Norn meanwhile gained influence, conquering Urabrask's and Sheoldred's domains, and Mirrans recruited constructs, golems and myr to the war.

nph.text: On Mirrodin, Karn's corrupted mind barked an order that the Phyrexians took as the command to begin the war on the surface.
The Mirran resistance fought bravely but in vain, and Koth sacrificed himself so a wounded Elspeth could escape.
Mirrans were broken down and rebuilt as loyal servants of the force they had fought, and Mirrodin was renamed New Phyrexia.

m12.text: Mirrodin had come under new management as Phyrexia took over, and visiting planeswalkers had to conclude that the Mirrans had lost the plane.

cmr.text: Sheoldred predicted that many worlds would bow to Phyrexia, with Mirrodin the first.
